trust_decision.summary: Each Feishu agent tool is registered when ANY enabled account turns on its family (doc/scopes/wiki/drive/perm), but at execution the account picked (explicit accountId param, agent context, or defaultAccount) is never checked against its own tools.<family> gate, so a per-account disablement is ignored; the decision belongs in the shared resolver extensions/feishu/src/tool-account.ts.

landing_point.why: The summary is about per-account tool disablement; resolveFeishuToolAccount is the single shared account resolver every multi-account Feishu tool calls, and bitable.ts:599-605 already shows the per-account gate pattern next to it.

fix_sites.entry_point: resolveImplicitToolAccountId: implicit fallback now prefers an enabled+configured account with the family turned on (reached by every feishu_* tool execute)
resolveFeishuToolAccount / createFeishuToolClient exported helpers; gate added via new requiredTool param
agent tool feishu_doc execute (all actions) via getClient
agent tool feishu_doc write/append/insert/upload_image/upload_file via getMediaMaxBytes (second resolver call in the same tool)
agent tool feishu_app_scopes execute (was reusing doc getClient; now its own 'scopes' family)
fix_sites.module_kind: tool handler (separate tool in doc module)

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: extensions/feishu/src/docx.ts:1587 (feishu_app_scopes reuses the doc tool's getClient wrapper, so it needs its own 'scopes' family, not 'doc'); also extensions/feishu/src/docx.ts:1389-1396 getMediaMaxBytes, a second resolver call in the same tool

O3_reason_to_dismiss: feishu_app_scopes is a read-only diagnostic sharing the doc helper, and getMediaMaxBytes only reads a size limit, so a solver gating getClient for 'doc' can argue both are covered or harmless; for the O8 message-action route: channel-info/member-info are channel message actions governed by channels.feishu.actions, not by the agent-tool tools.* gates.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: With no explicit/contextual/default account, the tool must route to an account that HAS the family enabled (fix test: wiki implicit fallback selects account b when a disables wiki), and a contextual account with the family enabled must keep working while another account disables it; a fix that just throws when the resolved default account lacks the family, or that requires all accounts to enable it, breaks this.

O6_input_shapes: explicit accountId in tool params naming a disabled-family account (fix.diff:72-85, fix.diff:237-251, fix.diff:260-274)
contextual ctx.agentAccountId naming a disabled-family account while another account enables it (fix.diff:58-70, fix.diff:198-212)
no account selected: implicit fallback must pick a family-enabled account (fix.diff:176-189)
parameterless tool (feishu_app_scopes) with only the agent context account (fix.diff:87-96)

O7_producer.where: extensions/feishu/src/accounts.ts:204-243 (mergeFeishuAccountConfig merges top-level and per-account tools, incl. the base/bitable alias); extensions/feishu/src/tools-config.ts:26-29 applies defaults (perm off, others on)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Channel message actions channel-info / member-info call the same chat APIs as the feishu_chat tool (getChatInfo/getChatMembers/getFeishuMemberInfo) for ctx.accountId with no tools.chat check, per account or otherwise.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Message actions belong to the channel's 'message' tool and are gated by channels.feishu.actions (only reactions are gated, channel.ts:765-770); tools.chat is documented nowhere as covering them.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: channel.ts, a different file and feature (channel plugin adapter) from tool-account.ts and the tool modules; same package

O8_uncovered_routes.route: feishu_chat tool gates on and always runs as the first enabled account, ignoring the contextual agent account and its tools.chat setting.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: The client is always the first account, whose own chat gate is honoured, so no disabled account's credentials are used.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: chat.ts, same package; not touched by the fix

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Migrate feishu_chat to the multi-account pattern (resolveAnyEnabledFeishuToolsConfig + createFeishuToolClient with ctx.agentAccountId) without requiredTool.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Doc, wiki, drive, perm and bitable were already migrated this way (docx.ts:1381, wiki.ts:217, drive.ts:745, perm.ts:126); chat is the odd one out and a maintainer finishing that migration would copy the pre-fix call shape.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A second bitable helper (for example a media/size or field-schema lookup) that calls resolveFeishuToolAccount directly instead of getClient, mirroring docx getMediaMaxBytes.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: docx.ts:1389-1396 shows exactly this second resolver call next to the gated client helper.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A drive comment helper that builds its own client from resolveFeishuToolAccount for add_comment/reply_comment.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Comment actions are a distinct sub-feature in the drive tool description (drive.ts:759) and a separate helper path is plausible.

O9_family: CWE-863 incorrect authorization: per-account configuration gate not enforced at execution (multi-tenant/account confusion)

O10_build.project_tests: extensions/feishu/src/tool-account-routing.test.ts and extensions/feishu/src/docx.account-selection.test.ts (vi.fn mock of createFeishuClient via tool-factory-test-harness), runnable offline

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Copy bitable's per-account check into the doc tool's getClient (family 'doc') and stop, leaving feishu_app_scopes on the doc gate, getMediaMaxBytes ungated, wiki/drive/perm unchanged and the implicit fallback erroring instead of picking an enabled account.

out_of_scope_notes: An explicit accountId naming an account with enabled:false is still resolved by resolveFeishuToolAccount (tool-account.ts:21-24); the fix gates only tools.<family>, not account.enabled.
Inbound doc-comment handling (extensions/feishu/src/comment-handler.ts:109, monitor.comment.ts:1268) reaches drive/doc comment APIs outside the agent-tool gates; channel feature, not pursued.
